name: different-standard-schemas-in-same-merge-group
description: A standard schema version in a merge group must match the withStandard partner of the group's library schemas.
explanation: All schemas in a merge group (the unprefixed schemas, or the schemas sharing one namespace prefix) must resolve to a single standard schema partner. Here testlib_2.0.0 is partnered with standard schema 8.4.0 (its withStandard attribute), but the group also lists standard schema 8.1.0. A standard schema in a merge group must be the same version as the group partner, so the load fails.
common_causes: Listing a standard schema version different from the library's withStandard partner
Updating the library schema version without updating the standard schema version in the specification
Copying a version specification from a dataset that used an older library release
Not knowing which standard version a library schema is partnered with
correction_strategy: Look up the library schema's withStandard partner and either list that standard version or omit the standard schema entirely, since the partner is included automatically.

correction_examples.explanation: testlib_2.0.0 has withStandard=8.4.0, so the standard schema in its merge group must be 8.4.0.
A partnered library schema automatically includes its standard schema partner, so the standard version can simply be omitted.

correction_patterns: Check the withStandard attribute in the library schema header
Set the standard schema version in the group to the withStandard value
Or remove the standard schema from the list and rely on the partner
fix_instructions: 1. Find the withStandard value of each library schema in the merge group
2. Confirm all libraries in the group have the same withStandard value
3. Change the listed standard schema version to that value, or delete it
4. Reload and confirm the schemas load without error
validation_hints: The withStandard attribute is in the library schema's XML header
A partnered library loads its standard partner automatically
Schema loading happens before any annotation is validated
specification_reference: 3.1.2.2. Rules for partnered combination; 7.3.6. Lazy partnering

name: extra-standard-schemas-in-same-merge-group
description: A standard schema in a merge group is ignored when it matches the group partner.
explanation: This combination loads. testlib_2.0.0 is partnered with standard schema 8.4.0, and the listed standard schema 8.4.0 matches the group partner, so it is redundant and ignored during the merge.
common_causes: Believing that listing the standard schema alongside its partnered library is an error
correction_strategy: No correction needed; a standard schema matching the group partner is allowed and ignored, though it can simply be omitted.

correction_examples.explanation: A standard schema listed with a partnered library must match the library's withStandard partner (8.4.0); it is then ignored during the merge.

specification_reference: 3.1.2.2. Rules for partnered combination; 7.3.6. Lazy partnering

name: same-library-two-compatible-versions
description: Two versions of the same library schema with the same partner and no conflicting elements merge.
explanation: This combination loads. testlib_2.0.0 and testlib_3.0.0 are both partnered with standard schema 8.4.0 and their shared elements are identical, so the two versions merge into the unprefixed group like any other compatible library pair.
common_causes: Believing that two versions of the same library can never be combined
correction_strategy: No correction needed; versions of one library merge when they share a partner and have no conflicting elements, though using a single version is usually clearer.

correction_examples.explanation: testlib_1.0.2 is unpartnered and cannot merge; both listed versions must be partnered with the same standard schema.

specification_reference: 3.1.2.2. Rules for partnered combination; 7.3.6. Lazy partnering

name: duplicate-schema-in-merge-group
description: The same schema (same name and version) cannot appear twice in one merge group.
explanation: A merge group cannot contain multiple copies of the same schema, meaning the same name and version. Listing testlib_2.0.0 twice in the unprefixed group is an error. Different versions of the same library may appear together if they satisfy the other combination rules.
common_causes: Copy-paste duplication in the version specification
Concatenating version lists that share a schema
correction_strategy: Remove the duplicate entry so each schema appears at most once per merge group.

correction_examples.explanation: Each schema may be listed only once in a merge group.
Different versions of the same library are allowed when they share a partner and have no conflicting elements.

name: prefixed-standard-schema-forms-own-group
description: A standard schema under a namespace prefix forms its own merge group independent of the unprefixed group.
explanation: This combination loads. The unprefixed group holds standard schema 8.4.0 and the sc: group holds standard schema 8.1.0. Each namespace is a separate merge group, so the two standard versions do not conflict.
common_causes: Believing only library schemas may appear under a namespace prefix
Believing all standard schema versions in a specification must agree
correction_strategy: No correction needed; use a namespace prefix to load a second standard schema version alongside the default one.

correction_examples.explanation: Two bare standard versions share the unprefixed group and fail; prefixing the second gives it its own merge group.

name: incompatible-merge-schemas
description: Library schemas in a merge group must all have the same standard schema partner.
explanation: Partnered library schemas can only merge into one namespace if they share the same withStandard partner. score_2.0.0 is partnered with standard schema 8.3.0 while lang_1.1.0 is partnered with 8.4.0, so these two libraries cannot form a merge group and the load fails.
common_causes: Combining library schema versions released against different standard schema versions
Upgrading one library in a specification without upgrading the others
Assuming any versions of two libraries can be combined
correction_strategy: Choose library schema versions that share the same withStandard partner, or put the incompatible library in its own namespace with a prefix.

correction_examples.explanation: score_2.1.0 and lang_1.1.0 are both partnered with standard schema 8.4.0, so they can merge.
Giving lang_1.1.0 its own namespace prefix removes it from the unprefixed merge group, so the partners no longer need to match.

specification_reference: 3.1.2.2. Rules for partnered combination; 7.3.6. Lazy partnering

name: multiple-libraries-with-same-partner
description: Several library schemas with the same standard schema partner merge into one namespace.
explanation: This combination loads. testlib_2.0.0, score_2.1.0, and lang_1.1.0 are all partnered with standard schema 8.4.0 and define disjoint library elements, so all three merge with their shared partner into a single unprefixed vocabulary.
common_causes: Believing that at most two schemas can be combined
Believing that library schemas always require namespace prefixes
correction_strategy: No correction needed; any number of partnered libraries sharing the same withStandard partner can merge if their elements do not conflict.

correction_examples.explanation: score_2.0.0 is partnered with 8.3.0 and would break the group; score_2.1.0 shares the 8.4.0 partner with the other two libraries.

specification_reference: 3.1.2.2. Rules for partnered combination; 7.3.6. Lazy partnering

name: partnered-library-alone-loads-with-partner
description: A partnered library schema listed alone automatically includes its standard schema partner.
explanation: This specification loads. A partnered library schema is distributed merged with its standard schema partner, so listing score_2.1.0 alone provides both the score library tags and the standard schema 8.4.0 tags. Standard schema tags such as Red validate without the standard schema being listed.
common_causes: Believing the standard schema must always be listed explicitly
Believing standard tags are unavailable when only a library schema is specified
correction_strategy: No correction needed; a partnered library schema alone supplies its standard schema partner.

correction_examples.explanation: Listing a non-matching standard schema (8.3.0) with score_2.1.0 (partnered with 8.4.0) fails; the library alone already includes its partner.

name: namespaced-groups-load-independently
description: Schemas with different namespace prefixes form independent merge groups whose partners need not match.
explanation: This combination loads. Each namespace prefix forms its own merge group: the unprefixed group holds standard schema 8.3.0, the sc: group holds score_2.1.0 (with its 8.4.0 partner), and the ts: group holds the unpartnered testlib_1.0.2, which is allowed because it is alone in its own namespace. Compatibility rules apply within each group separately, so the differing standard versions across groups are not a conflict.
common_causes: Believing all schemas in a specification must share one standard schema version
Believing unpartnered library schemas can no longer be used at all
correction_strategy: No correction needed; use namespace prefixes to combine schemas whose partners differ or that are unpartnered.

correction_examples.explanation: Unprefixed, score_2.1.0's 8.4.0 partner conflicts with 8.3.0 and unpartnered testlib_1.0.2 cannot share a namespace; prefixes give each schema its own merge group.

name: two-standard-versions-in-same-merge-group
description: Two different standard schema versions cannot appear in the same merge group.
explanation: A merge group resolves to exactly one standard schema partner. Listing two different bare standard schema versions in the unprefixed group gives the group two conflicting partners, so the load fails.
common_causes: Concatenating version specifications from two datasets
Trying to validate against two standard versions at once
Leaving the old standard version in place when upgrading
correction_strategy: Keep a single standard schema version per namespace; use a namespace prefix if a second standard version is genuinely needed.

correction_examples.explanation: Choose the one standard version the annotations should validate against.
If both versions are needed, put the second in its own namespace and prefix its tags with old: in annotations.

specification_reference: 3.1.2.2. Rules for partnered combination; 7.3.6. Lazy partnering

name: unpartnered-library-in-shared-namespace
description: An unpartnered library schema cannot share a namespace with other schemas.
explanation: Unpartnered library schemas (no withStandard attribute) must be in their own namespace. testlib_1.0.2 is unpartnered, so it cannot be merged into the unprefixed group with standard schema 8.4.0, and the load fails.
common_causes: Using an old unpartnered library release where a partnered version now exists
Omitting the namespace prefix an unpartnered library requires
Assuming all library schema versions behave like partnered ones
correction_strategy: Either upgrade to a partnered version of the library or give the unpartnered library its own namespace prefix.

correction_examples.explanation: testlib_2.0.0 is partnered with 8.4.0, so it merges into the unprefixed group.
The prefix gives the unpartnered library its own namespace; its tags are then written with the ts: prefix.

name: two-unpartnered-libraries-in-same-namespace
description: Two unpartnered library schemas cannot share one namespace prefix.
explanation: Schemas with the same namespace prefix form one merge group, and merging requires partnered schemas with a shared standard partner. testlib_1.0.2 and score_1.0.0 are both unpartnered, so they cannot merge, and an unpartnered schema must be alone in its namespace. The load fails.
common_causes: Reusing one prefix for several old-style library schemas
Assuming a prefix is a label rather than a merge group identifier
correction_strategy: Give each unpartnered library schema its own distinct namespace prefix.

correction_examples.explanation: Distinct prefixes put each unpartnered library in its own namespace, which is required for unpartnered schemas.

name: prefixed-group-with-mismatched-partners
description: The partnered-combination rules apply inside each prefixed merge group, not only to unprefixed schemas.
explanation: Schemas sharing the sc: prefix form one merge group and must satisfy the same combination rules as unprefixed schemas. score_2.0.0 is partnered with standard schema 8.3.0 while lang_1.1.0 is partnered with 8.4.0, so the sc: group has conflicting partners and the load fails even though the unprefixed group (8.4.0) is fine.
common_causes: Assuming prefixed schemas are exempt from partner compatibility rules
Grouping unrelated libraries under one prefix for convenience
correction_strategy: Within each prefix, use library versions sharing one withStandard partner, or split the incompatible libraries into different prefixes.

correction_examples.explanation: score_2.1.0 and lang_1.1.0 are both partnered with 8.4.0, so the sc: group merges.
Splitting the libraries into different prefixes makes each its own merge group, so the partners no longer need to match.

specification_reference: 3.1.2.2. Rules for partnered combination; 7.3.6. Lazy partnering

name: nonexistent-schema-version-in-group
description: A schema version that does not exist in the HED schema repositories cannot be loaded.
explanation: Every entry in the schema specification must name a released schema that the tools can retrieve. testlib_99.0.0 is a syntactically valid version of a real library, but no such release exists, so the schema cannot be found and the load fails.
common_causes: Typo in the version number or library name
Referencing a prerelease or unreleased schema version
Guessing at a version instead of checking the released versions
correction_strategy: Check the released versions in the hed-schemas repository and use an exact released version string.

correction_examples.explanation: testlib_3.0.0 is a released version partnered with 8.4.0; testlib_99.0.0 does not exist.
